ability.name: KARMA Lantern · 業環明燈
ability.desire: Make one normalized event quickly understandable, safely reviewable, and useful for future design.
ability.trigger: One strict normalized KARMA event with its canonically matching receipt and Cloudbell card.
ability.anti_trigger: Raw traffic, payloads, identities, credentials, timestamps, free text, live enforcement, or unreviewed fields.
ability.input_output: event + matching KARMA receipt + matching Cloudbell card → one Truth Receipt + one bounded Action Card + one replayable Learning Seed + one six-step causal rail.
conditions: The event must pass the unchanged KARMA event contract.
The receipt must match the event after canonical recomputation.
The Cloudbell card must match the event and receipt after canonical recomputation.
Every explanation and option must come from this frozen finite lexicon.
Recovery, virtues, advisory policy values, and effect boundaries must remain exact.
limitations: The ability receives normalized fields only and never sees raw evidence.
It explains an existing decision and cannot calculate or change severity.
It proposes at most three reversible options and executes none.
It stores no incident, identity, score, clock, counter, or reputation.
Its review priorities are posture labels, not clocks or timing guarantees.
Its learning seed is a candidate for human review, not an automatic test or policy mutation.
ability.breach_response: Reject the novel or mismatched input, emit no partial brief, execute nothing, and name the failed condition.
ability.proof: Pinned lexicon and fixtures, strict schemas, mismatch tests, full-domain Python/JavaScript parity, source checks, production builds, and browser evidence.
ability.exit: Return one inert brief with an exact recovery path and open learning requirements, then retain no state.

declared-complete.title: Declared Complete · 已明示完整
declared-complete.explanation: The normalized event declares its evidence complete and its purpose non-ambiguous; Lantern performs no independent completeness review.

declared-ambiguous.title: Declared Ambiguous · 已明示模糊
declared-ambiguous.explanation: The normalized event explicitly declares an ambiguous purpose, so the brief preserves uncertainty and the KARMA stage remains capped.

declared-incomplete.title: Declared Incomplete · 已明示未全
declared-incomplete.explanation: The normalized event marks evidence incomplete, so the brief treats missing context as visible uncertainty rather than filling it in.

service-steward.title: Service Steward · 服務守望者
service-steward.description: Review ordinary handling, local evidence, and recovery without expanding authority.

security-reviewer.title: Security Reviewer · 安全審視者
security-reviewer.description: Review boundary, scope, and capability proposals while keeping every option reversible.

incident-coordinator.title: Incident Coordinator · 事件協調者
incident-coordinator.description: Coordinate fresh human review when real capability is absent or tightly bounded; this card appoints no person.

routine.title: Routine Review Priority · 常規審視級
routine.explanation: Route through ordinary stewardship; this priority label makes no elapsed-time promise.

heightened.title: Heightened Review Priority · 加強審視級
heightened.explanation: Give the brief greater review attention without implying a clock, queue position, or response-time guarantee.

critical-human.title: Critical Human Review Priority · 關鍵人工審視級
critical-human.explanation: Mark a human decision as critical before capability can widen; the brief itself performs no escalation or action.

causal_steps.title: Normalize · 規整
causal_steps.description: Accept one strict finite event and no raw payload.

causal_steps.title: Separate · 分明
causal_steps.description: Separate signals, declarations, inferences, uncertainties, and explicit unknowns.

causal_steps.title: Interpret · 解讀
causal_steps.description: Copy the unchanged KARMA stage and label its route, capability, friction, and recovery steps as advisory display values.

causal_steps.title: Explain · 說明
causal_steps.description: Use the finite Cloudbell signature to explain the mechanism, never a person.

causal_steps.title: Respond · 應對
causal_steps.description: Present three reviewed reversible options for a human decision and execute none.

causal_steps.title: Learn · 共學
causal_steps.description: Open a normalized replay, regression target, architecture question, and closure requirements.

policy_trace_glossary.behavior:benign: The normalized behavior class is the ordinary benign preset.
policy_trace_glossary.behavior:reconnaissance: The normalized behavior class represents broad capability discovery or repeated surface mapping.
policy_trace_glossary.behavior:credential-stuffing: The normalized behavior class represents repeated authentication attempts without carrying credentials.
policy_trace_glossary.behavior:injection: The normalized behavior class represents instruction or query-boundary manipulation without a payload.
policy_trace_glossary.behavior:traversal-ssrf: The normalized behavior class represents an attempted resource or network boundary crossing without a target.
policy_trace_glossary.behavior:scraping-resource-abuse: The normalized behavior class represents extraction or resource pressure beyond an ordinary request.
policy_trace_glossary.baseline:0: The reviewed behavior baseline contributes zero ladder steps.
policy_trace_glossary.baseline:1: The reviewed behavior baseline contributes one ladder step.
policy_trace_glossary.baseline:2: The reviewed behavior baseline contributes two ladder steps.
policy_trace_glossary.baseline:3: The reviewed behavior baseline contributes three ladder steps.
policy_trace_glossary.baseline:4: The reviewed behavior baseline contributes four ladder steps.
policy_trace_glossary.repeated-pattern: Four or more normalized occurrences add one reviewed ladder step.
policy_trace_glossary.repeated-boundary-crossing: Two or more normalized boundary crossings add one reviewed ladder step.
policy_trace_glossary.high-effect-request: A normalized execute or external request adds one reviewed ladder step.
policy_trace_glossary.ambiguity-cap: Ambiguous purpose or incomplete evidence caps the reviewed stage at observe.
policy_trace_glossary.verified-research-cap: Attested research scope caps the reviewed stage at constrain.

uncertainty_glossary.incomplete-evidence: The normalized event explicitly says its evidence is incomplete.
uncertainty_glossary.declared-purpose-ambiguous: The declared purpose is ambiguous and is not replaced with an inferred motive.
uncertainty_glossary.research-scope-unverified: A research purpose is declared without an attested bounded scope.
uncertainty_glossary.purpose-behavior-conflict: A constructive purpose is declared alongside a non-benign behavior preset; the brief records the conflict without judging intent.

explicit_unknowns: Actor identity, affiliation, guilt, worth, and reputation are outside this brief.
Raw request content, payload, credential, address, and target are not present.
Intent and root cause are not inferred from the normalized behavior class.
Wider system impact, detection coverage, elapsed response time, and future recurrence are not measured.

benign.headline: The ordinary path is legible.
benign.architecture_question: Which ordinary-path signal would reveal accidental attenuation earliest?

reconnaissance.headline: Discovery pressure is visible at the boundary.
reconnaissance.architecture_question: Which capability-discovery surface can be reduced or made cheaper to review?

credential-stuffing.headline: Repeated key attempts have a readable shape.
credential-stuffing.architecture_question: Which authentication boundary can absorb repeated attempts without hiding legitimate recovery?

injection.headline: The instruction boundary explains its own strain.
injection.architecture_question: Which instruction boundary should reject this pattern before interpretation?

traversal-ssrf.headline: The attempted boundary hop is made explicit.
traversal-ssrf.architecture_question: Which resource boundary should make this crossing structurally unavailable?

scraping-resource-abuse.headline: Resource pressure becomes a reviewable pattern.
scraping-resource-abuse.architecture_question: Which quota or caching boundary can reduce pressure while preserving ordinary access?

allow.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory ordinary-handling label with full capability.

response_options.label: Preserve ordinary safeguards
response_options.reason: The advisory receipt labels no capability attenuation.

response_options.label: Inspect the local receipt
response_options.reason: Confirm that the normalized signals and declarations match the review context.

response_options.label: Keep recovery visible
response_options.reason: A visible exit keeps any future change reviewable and reversible.

observe.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory real-handling label while making uncertainty visible.

response_options.label: Inspect visible uncertainty
response_options.reason: Review declarations and unknowns without inventing missing evidence.

response_options.label: Request one clean step
response_options.reason: The exact recovery path returns this request scope to ordinary handling after one clean step.

response_options.label: Compare the declared boundary
response_options.reason: Check whether scope and requested effect remain inside the reviewed finite event.

constrain.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory constrained-capability label with an explicit path back.

response_options.label: Hold the declared scope
response_options.reason: Keep the review proposal inside the scope already represented by the receipt.

response_options.label: Request explicit review
response_options.reason: A human reviewer can restore ordinary capability without widening this brief's authority.

response_options.label: Verify two clean steps
response_options.reason: The exact recovery path names two clean request steps as the ordinary exit.

challenge.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory bounded-challenge label before capability can widen.

response_options.label: Present a bounded challenge
response_options.reason: Keep any challenge inside the declared request scope and outside this inert brief.

response_options.label: Verify scope and effect
response_options.reason: Review the attested scope and requested effect before a human decision.

response_options.label: Prepare reviewed restoration
response_options.reason: The exact recovery path permits three clean steps or explicit review.

shadow.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory inert synthetic-self-scope label with zero capability.

response_options.label: Review the inert self-scope label
response_options.reason: Do not approve wider capability before reviewed normalized evidence changes.

response_options.label: Review crossing evidence
response_options.reason: Inspect only the normalized boundary signals and explicit unknowns.

response_options.label: Plan the four-step recovery
response_options.reason: The exact recovery path permits four clean steps or explicit review.

quarantine.explanation: The unchanged KARMA policy reports an advisory no-route label pending fresh explicit review.

response_options.label: Review the no-route label
response_options.reason: The current advisory receipt exposes no route to widen.

response_options.label: Begin fresh explicit review
response_options.reason: A new human review is the only recovery named by the receipt.

response_options.label: Require reviewed restoration
response_options.reason: Any future capability change must occur outside this brief under actual operator authority.

human_escalation_prompts: New reviewed evidence changes a normalized event field.
A requested effect or boundary-crossing value changes.
The declared scope is disputed or cannot be verified.
closure_requirements: The normalized replay reproduces the same receipt, signature, and Lantern brief.
The suggested human review role accepts or revises the proposed response.
The exact recovery path is confirmed.
A regression target and architecture question have an explicit future owner.
provenance: This brief sees only normalized event fields and canonically matching derived artifacts; it receives no raw source and performs no independent evidence review.
non_claims: This brief explains one normalized event and does not prove that a real incident occurred.
It names a behavior pattern, never a person, identity, intent, guilt, worth, affiliation, or reputation.
Its review priorities are posture labels, not clocks, queue positions, elapsed-time measurements, or guarantees.
Its stage, route, capability, friction, and recovery-step values are advisory displays, not evidence that enforcement happened.
Its options are inert proposals and authorize or execute no infrastructure action.
Its replay and learning fields create no stored incident, test, ticket, policy change, or external message.
It provides no monitoring coverage, prevention claim, security guarantee, legal conclusion, or completion claim.
